hints: Take natural logarithms of $ky = \mathrm{e}^{cx}$ to obtain the linear equation $\ln y = cx - \ln k$.
Calculate gradient $c$ using the points $(2.80, 0.372)$ and $(5.10, 2.21)$, then solve for $k$ to 2 significant figures.
walkthrough:
Take natural logarithms of both sides of $ky = \mathrm{e}^{cx}$:
$$\ln(ky) = \ln\left(\mathrm{e}^{cx}\right)$$
$$\ln k + \ln y = cx$$
$$\ln y = cx - \ln k$$

Identify this with the straight-line equation $Y = mX + C$ where $Y = \ln y$ and $X = x$:
$$\text{Gradient } m = c$$
$$\text{Vertical intercept } C = -\ln k$$

Calculate the gradient $c$ using the coordinates $(x_1, y_1) = (2.80, 0.372)$ and $(x_2, y_2) = (5.10, 2.21)$:
$$c = \dfrac{2.21 - 0.372}{5.10 - 2.80} = \dfrac{1.838}{2.30} \approx 0.7991304 \dots$$
